content: Evaluations of antiviral effectiveness, safety, resistance, and vaccine coverage, as well as their effectiveness and safety, should be conducted throughout their deployment in alignment with national plans, mechanisms, and procedures. Recovery activities should be based on national or local risk assessments, available resources, and identified needs. These activities include: 1. Conducting a comprehensive evaluation of all specific responses and interventions, such as: The effectiveness, safety, and resistance of antiviral treatments. Vaccine coverage, effectiveness, and safety. Sharing findings with the international community. 2. Rebuilding essential services to prepare for subsequent waves of disease or other health emergencies. 3. Increasing seasonal influenza vaccine coverage among all high-risk groups, as per national policies. Preparedness activities should also be guided by national or local risk assessments, resources, and needs. These include: 1. Identifying non-pharmaceutical interventions that may be recommended and developing protocols and communication strategies to support their implementation. 2. 3. Response activities should also be considered based on risk assessments, resources, and needs. These include: 1. Assessing whether cancellation, restriction, or modification of mass gatherings is necessary. 2. 3. Community-level preparedness activities should focus on: 1. Developing guidance and plans to support prevention, treatment, and infection control for individuals isolated at home and their household contacts. 2. Creating mechanisms to increase access to treatment and care for community members. 3. Launching public health education campaigns, including targeted messaging and feedback mechanisms for disadvantaged or hard-to-reach groups. Response activities at the community level should include: 1. 2. 3. Advising household contacts to minimize interactions outside the home and isolate themselves at the first signs of influenza symptoms. 4. Encouraging individuals to stay home when ill and providing infection control guidance for household caregivers, following WHO recommendations. Recovery activities should also include providing psychosocial services to support individual and community-level recovery as needed. The WHO guidance document on pandemic influenza risk management has been developed based on prior guidance and reviewed by technical experts. It incorporates feedback from internal and external peer review groups, ensuring its relevance and applicability.
